requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-002 and trace-animals-fit-p10-005 show the same heading and title today.

requirements.statement: The heading carries the caption 'About the consignment'.
requirements.why: DR2.1 uses this caption, even though the hub places the row under '2. Description of the goods'; today's page already matches DR2.1.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p10-008 shows the caption 'About the consignment' today.

requirements.statement: Inset text under the heading reads 'You must add all animal identification details before the consignment arrives at the port of entry.'
requirements.why: Tells the trader identification can follow later but must be in before arrival; both versions already say it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-004 holds the same inset text.

requirements.statement: Above the heading, the page shows the notification status strip: the status tag and the notification reference.

requirements.statement: The Alpha phase banner and its feedback link on this page.
requirements.why: Out of this area: the phase banner is shared page furniture decided by the layout-and-sign-in area; recorded here only so the claim is weighed.

requirements.statement: The page's 'Back' link goes to the Commodity details page (consignment details) in the linear journey; when the page was opened from the hub, review or template review, the journey's own back-link rule applies.
requirements.why: DR2.1 places identification straight after commodity details, so Back returns there; the prototype wins by default.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the back link always returns to the notification Overview (repo-frontend-p6-005, trace-animals-fit-p10-012).

requirements.statement: The page is a journey step only when at least one selected species has identifier fields. Commodity details then continues to it; otherwise the journey skips it, and a direct GET or POST to it redirects to the next step after Commodity details.
requirements.why: DR2.1 puts identification in the linear flow after commodity details and skips it when there is nothing to identify (poultry, fish).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page is reached only from the Overview's task row, and a direct visit with nothing to identify redirects to the Overview (trace-e2e-p6-004, repo-frontend-p6-009), not to the next journey step.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, 'Save and continue' on a valid identification page reached through the journey goes to the next journey page: Additional details where that page applies, otherwise Arrival details. When the page was opened from its overview task, the review or template review, it returns there instead.
requirements.why: DR2.1 runs the journey page to page. The 9 October ruling splits this requirement into a live half (this one) and a germinal half, and confirms that a page opened from its overview task returns to the overview on Save and continue, with no new from-hub marker.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Save and continue always redirects to the Overview (trace-animals-fit-p10-079, trace-e2e-p6-057), even when the trader came through the journey from Commodity details.

requirements.statement: The page ends with the shared journey actions: 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to overview' (saves, then returns to the overview) and the link 'Cancel and return to overview', with the amend and template-review variants the journey uses elsewhere.
requirements.why: Both versions end the page on the same three controls.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p10-077 shows the same button group today; the amend and template variants belong to the journey-flow and templates areas.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' save the typed identifiers only for species with one animal; values typed into the form of a species with more than one animal are not saved unless its own panel button was pressed.
requirements.why: DR2.1 saves a multi-animal species only through its 'Save and add another' / 'Save and finish' button. The 9 October ruling splits this requirement; the germinal half is req-250.
requirements.deltaNote: Today any save, the page's Save and continue included, saves one new record for every card whose form holds data (repo-frontend-p6-072, trace-animals-fit-p10-080).

requirements.statement: A species panel's own save button validates and saves only that species' current animal, then reloads the page showing that species' next animal; other species' forms are neither checked nor saved.
requirements.why: DR2.1 saves one species' animal at a time; today one button saves and validates every card on the page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an in-card add validates every open card and appends a record for every card holding data, card by card, so one card's failure can leave earlier cards' records saved (repo-frontend-p6-073, repo-frontend-p6-079-m1).

requirements.statement: Pressing Enter in a field submits the page as 'Save and continue', never as a species panel's save, through the hidden default submit button at the top of the form (visually hidden, aria-hidden, not focusable).
requirements.why: A real-service safeguard DR2.1 does not show: without it Enter would press the first panel or Remove button. DR2.1 shows no other way to do the same job, so it is kept.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-076 and trace-e2e-p6-060 show the hidden default 'finish' button today.

requirements.statement: The page keeps the real service's mechanics: its address under the notification (commodities/identification), its entry guard, a CSRF crumb and concurrency token on every post, server-side validation only, values that fail validation never saved, and errors shown only on the response to the failing submission.
requirements.why: Persistence, authentication and validation are real constraints the prototype cannot express, and the ruling lets them override it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-073 and trace-animals-fit-p11-001 show today's server-side re-render without saving; repo-frontend-p6-077 the crumb and token; repo-perftests-p1-025 shows the k6 suite already driving the page at commodities/identification.

requirements.statement: The 'Selected commodities' summary has one row per selected commodity with the columns 'Commodity code', 'Common name', 'Species' and the quantity column; a commodity with several species lists each species on its own line in the Species cell, and the quantity cell shows the row's number of animals.

requirements.deltaNote: Today the table has no Species column and shows one row per commodity line, each line one species (trace-animals-fit-p10-014, trace-animals-fit-p10-017-m1).

requirements.statement: The summary's 'Common name' and the commodity section heading name the commodity the same way (DR2.1: 'Cattle' in the summary and 'Cattle (0102)' as the heading).
requirements.why: Today the same cattle line is 'Domestic cattle' in the summary and 'Cow' on its card, which reads as two different things.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the summary shows the species' common name ('Domestic cattle') and the card the commodity name ('Cow') for the same line (trace-e2e-p6-014).

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, the summary's quantity column is headed 'Number of animals'.
requirements.why: DR2.1 heads the column 'Number of animals' whenever any live animal is selected. Each set now holds one category and the live catalogue loses its germinal lines, so the live set never shows 'Number of packages'; the 9 October ruling splits this requirement, and the germinal half is req-1776.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-095 and trace-animals-fit-p10-014 show the column headed 'Number of animals' today.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-098 shows the link today.

requirements.statement: Identification is grouped into one section per commodity headed '<commodity name> (<commodity code>)', such as 'Cattle (0102)', and inside it one panel per selected species with identifier fields, in selection order, headed with the species name (such as 'Bos taurus').
requirements.why: DR2.1 separates the commodity heading from the species panel, replacing today's single card heading.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each commodity line is one card headed '<name> (<code>) — <species>', such as 'Cow (0102) — Bos taurus' (trace-e2e-p6-015).

requirements.statement: Each species panel has a 'Change number of animals' link (visually hidden suffix naming the panel) to the Commodity details page.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-060 and trace-animals-fit-p10-025 show the link on every card today.

requirements.why: DR2.1 has nothing to count against until the number is given.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a line with no declared count still gets a card with the uncapped counter 'Enter details for {species}' (repo-frontend-p6-063).

requirements.why: DR2.1 falls back to these commodities' own identifier, the ear tag; it applies once the commodities area offers them. The 9 October afternoon ruling holds inc-051 with the commodity catalogue: none of these commodities is in today's five-commodity live catalogue, and the catalogue waits on MDM.
requirements.blockedBy: Commodities come from MDM: pigs, sheep and goats join the live-animals catalogue only through the MDM commodity integration, which this programme cannot build (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm, claims p2-005 and p2-025).

requirements.statement: The ear tag field has no hint.

requirements.statement: Each live-animal identifier (microchip, passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name) is limited to 58 characters.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so the real limit stays although DR2.1 sets none for these fields.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-020 sets IDENTIFIER_MAX_LENGTH = 58 today.

requirements.statement: Live-animal identifier length errors use DR2.1's wording, '<label> must be 58 characters or less': 'Microchip must be 58 characters or less', 'Passport must be 58 characters or less', 'Tattoo must be 58 characters or less', 'Ear tag must be 58 characters or less' and 'Horse name must be 58 characters or less'.
requirements.why: Where a real rule is kept, DR2.1's wording for the same kind of rule is used; it also matches the address-length errors' 'or less'.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the messages say 'characters or fewer' (repo-frontend-p6-021 to p6-025).

requirements.statement: Identifier values are trimmed of surrounding spaces before they are checked and saved, so surrounding spaces never count towards the length limit.
requirements.why: DR2.1 trims before checking; today trims only what it saves.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the length limit is checked against the untrimmed value (repo-frontend-p6-026-m1).

requirements.statement: Each identifier error appears in an error summary titled 'There is a problem', in field order, linking to and focusing its own field (field ids unique per commodity line and field, in the real service's naming), and inline on the field in error.
requirements.why: Both versions link each error to the field it is about. Field names and ids are architecture, which the prototype never decides (c-039), so today's per-line ids stay; with one line per species they are already unique per species.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p11-004 and p11-005 show summary links that focus the field and inline errors today, with per-line field ids (repo-frontend-p6-018).

requirements.statement: When a save fails validation, the page is shown again with the values the user typed kept in the form.
requirements.why: Both versions keep what the trader typed.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p6-043 shows typed values kept after a failed add today.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, an animal counts as entered once at least one identifier its species asks for has a value: it is saved, listed in the saved-animals table and the panel moves on to the next animal, with the other identifiers left blank.
requirements.why: Sam's 9 October ruling: one identifier is enough, for the Complete status and for submit, and DR1 inc-103 (every identifier filled) is closed and not built. It holds 'for now' on the footing that it is no change, which today's service confirms.
requirements.deltaNote: Today one identifier is enough: a cow with only an ear tag and a dog with only a microchip are saved and listed (trace-e2e-p6-102, trace-animals-fit-p10-065, repo-frontend-p6-019).

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, pressing a species panel's 'Save and add another' or 'Save and finish' with every identifier of the current animal blank saves nothing and shows 'Enter at least one identifier for this animal' in the error summary and inline, linked to that panel's first identifier field. The check is made per panel, so an empty panel is refused even when another species' form holds data. A partly filled animal saves with no error. The page's 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' never block on missing identifiers: an empty form saves no record and the trader moves on, and the page shows no message about the submit rule.
requirements.why: One identifier is enough (9 October ruling), so DR1's per-identifier errors, which it asked for only if every identifier were ruled required, are not built. An animal with no identifier at all is not a record, and validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so today's at-least-one error stays where DR2.1 silently keeps the trader on the same animal (c-042).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the message, its link and the partial save exist (repo-frontend-p6-027, trace-animals-fit-p11-006), but the empty check fires only when no card anywhere on the page holds data, so an empty card beside a filled one is skipped silently (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p5-019).

requirements.statement: The saved-animals table lists every saved animal, including one saved with only some of its identifiers; an identifier left blank shows as an empty cell.
requirements.why: A record with one identifier counts as identified (9 October ruling), so it is listed like any other; DR2.1's complete-only listing rested on its every-identifier rule, which the ruling sets aside (c-041).
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p10-063 and trace-e2e-p6-048 show every saved record listed today, with empty cells for identifiers left blank.

requirements.statement: The saved-animals table sits below the entry form and the panel save button, and shows both while animals are still being entered and once all are entered.
requirements.why: DR2.1's order puts the next animal's form first.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the table sits above the entry form (repo-frontend-p6-084, trace-animals-fit-p10-058).

requirements.statement: The saved-animals table has an 'Animal' column, one column per identifier the species asks for (headed with the field label), and a Remove action; each row is labelled '<species> <n>', such as 'Bos taurus 1'.
requirements.why: Both versions show saved animals this way.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p10-060 and p10-061 show the Animal column, identifier columns and '<species> <n>' rows today.

requirements.statement: Each saved row has a 'Remove' button (visually hidden suffix 'animal <n>') that posts the form, deletes that animal straight away with no confirmation, renumbers later animals, reopens the entry form for the freed place, and deletes the species' identification record when its last animal is removed.
requirements.why: Both versions remove a saved animal in one step.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p10-069 and p10-071 show Remove deleting with no confirmation and reopening the form today.

requirements.statement: A saved animal cannot be changed in place: correcting one means removing it and entering it again.
requirements.why: Both versions offer only Remove on a saved row.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p10-070 shows only Remove on saved rows today.

requirements.statement: When every animal of a species is entered, the panel shows only the saved-animals table: no entry form, no panel button and no completion message.
requirements.why: DR2.1 shows the table alone; today's 'You have entered details for all...' line is copy DR2.1 leaves out (and its 'all 1 ... animals' wording is ungrammatical).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the card shows 'You have entered details for all {count} {species} animals. Remove a record if you need to replace it.' (repo-frontend-p6-065).

requirements.statement: For live animals each panel takes one animal at a time under the heading 'Enter details for <species> <n> of <total>', where n is the first animal not yet entered and total the species' number of animals.
requirements.why: Both versions identify one animal at a time against the declared count.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-062 and trace-e2e-p6-019 show the same counter today.

requirements.statement: A species with more than one animal has a panel button 'Save and add another', reading 'Save and finish' on the last animal still to enter; a species with one animal has no panel button and is saved by the page's own buttons.
requirements.why: Both versions word the panel button by what is left to enter.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-068 and p6-069 implement the same wording and the no-button single animal today.

requirements.statement: The panel's 'Save and add another' / 'Save and finish' button is a primary (green) button.
requirements.why: DR2.1 renders it as a primary button.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the in-card button is secondary (repo-frontend-p6-070).

requirements.statement: A panel save is a full page post that redirects back to the page, where the form is empty for the next animal.
requirements.why: Both versions reload the page after each animal, and every state change being a form post keeps the page working without JavaScript, as the 9 October afternoon ruling requires.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p10-055 shows the 302 back to the page and trace-e2e-p6-044-m2 the empty form today.

requirements.statement: A stale panel save for a species with every animal already entered saves nothing and shows 'You have already entered details for all <count> animals — remove a record before adding another', linked to the species panel; a Remove naming an animal that does not exist is refused (400) before anything is deleted.
requirements.why: Stale forms and concurrent edits are real persistence constraints the prototype cannot express; the ruling lets them override its silent no-op.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-078 and trace-animals-fit-p10-072 show the cap-reached error today; repo-frontend-p6-092 the 400.

requirements.statement: If a species ever holds more saved animals than its number of animals, its panel hides the entry form and shows 'This commodity line lists <count> <species> animals but you have entered details for <records>. Remove <excess> to continue.'
requirements.why: The safety net behind DR1's count-drop judgement: entered data is never silently orphaned.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-066 renders this message today.

requirements.statement: Lowering a species' number of animals on Commodity details below its saved identification records is refused with 'You have 2 identifier records for Bos taurus but entered 1 animal. Remove identifier records or keep the higher count.', and the error summary link goes to that species' panel on this page.
requirements.why: DR1 judged this same difference (inc-094, Sam 2026-08-21): DR2.1 orphans the surplus records silently.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p6-061 and trace-animals-fit-p10-075 show the refusal and the link to the card today; the anchor follows the species panel once req-213 lands.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, the hub's Identification details row shows Complete on exactly the bar the notification must meet to submit (req-249), counting a saved animal with at least one identifier as identified: with one species selected it is Complete straight away; with several, it is Complete once each species with identifier fields has at least one such animal. There is no stricter bar, such as every animal of every species entered.
requirements.why: Sam's 9 October ruling: one identifier is enough for the Complete status and for submit, and there is no separate, stricter bar for Complete. That sets aside DR2.1's every-animal-complete rule (c-041) and matches what the service does today.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a single-species consignment shows Complete straight after Commodity details (trace-animals-fit-p10-003-m1, trace-e2e-p6-002) and stays Complete at 1 of 2 (trace-e2e-p6-066), while a two-species consignment shows To do before any record (trace-animals-fit-p10-002); the ruling records this as what the code does today.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, to submit: identification details are optional when only one species is selected; when more than one species is selected, each species with identifier fields needs at least one saved animal with at least one identifier. The identification page itself shows no message for this rule.
requirements.why: DR2.1's and DR1's minimum-identifier rule for submitting, with 'complete' read as one identifier per the 9 October ruling, which records it as the rule DR1 inc-100 built. The ruling leaves the wording of the several-lines rule to the Behaviour Spec; the review-and-submit area owns the gate and its message. The 9 October ruling splits this requirement; the germinal half is req-261.
requirements.deltaNote: ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-188 records the one-identifier rule as what the code does today (DR1 inc-100); trace-animals-fit-p10-003-m1 and p10-002 show the hub status already following the one-species and several-species halves of it.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set's identification page, Collection date and Production date are each a single text input with the hint 'For example, 27/03/2026', which works without JavaScript; no range rule applies to either date, and the production date is not checked against the collection date.
requirements.why: DR2.1's date fields for germinal products, built in the germinal set's copy of the page (9 October ruling). conflicts.about: Whether the page takes the prototype's mount mechanics (its own URL, no entry guards, errors held in the session, invalid values saved).

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence, validation or authentication, overrides the prototype.
The page is served at /animal-identification-details under /design-release-2.1.
The page has no entry guards and can be opened at any point.
Errors are held in the session and shown again on reload.
Values that fail validation are written to the session before errors are shown.
Each identifier field is named identifiers[<species id>][<field id>] with the id identifier-<species id>-<field id>.
The prototype never decides architecture: URL paths, query parameter and form field names, data-model shape or code structure.
If any card has an error nothing is saved and the page re-renders with the values kept.

conflicts.outcome: Both rulings rank first. The 7 October ruling names persistence, validation and authentication as constraints that override the prototype, and the 9 October ruling keeps this conflict for that reason and adds that the prototype never decides URL paths or form field names. The page keeps the real address under its notification, its guard, CSRF and concurrency token and its own field names and ids, and never saves invalid values or replays errors from the session.

conflicts.about: Whether the real identifier validation and stale-action safeguards stay where DR2.1 has none.

positions.says: Validation and persistence are real constraints that override the prototype.
A live-animal identifier with no length limit is never rejected for its content.
A panel save for a species with no animal left to enter does nothing and returns to the page.
A remove request for a position that does not exist is ignored.
Each identifier value can be at most 58 characters.
An add for a card already at its cap saves nothing and shows the cap-reached error.
A remove naming a record that does not exist is refused with 400.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the 58-character identifier limit, the cap-reached error for a stale add and the 400 for a bad remove stay. Where DR2.1 words the same kind of rule, its wording is used: '<label> must be 58 characters or less'. prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-066 is not overruled: its other half (removing the last animal deletes the species' record) still stands.

conflicts.about: When an animal (or a germinal entry) counts as identified, and what bar the Complete status sets: one identifier filled, or every identifier its species asks for and every animal entered.

positions.says: One identifier is enough: a record with one identifier counts as identified, for the Complete status and for submit.
There is no separate, stricter bar for the Complete status than for submit.
DR1 inc-103 (counting an animal as identified only once every identifier is filled in) is closed and not built.
The prototype wins by default; only a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint overrides it.
An animal's entry counts as complete only when every identifier field for its species has a value.
The saved-animals table shows only complete entries; a partly filled entry is not listed.
Identification is complete only when every animal of every species with fields is saved and complete; a germinal species only needs its one entry to exist.
A cattle animal is saved only when both Ear tag and Passport are filled in.
No single identifier is mandatory; one identifier is enough to save an animal.
Design release 1 holds a trader on an animal until every identifier for that commodity has a value.
Whether DR1's every-identifier rule or V4's at-least-one rule governs inc-103 is undecided; only the design authority can say.
inc-103 is deferred, held for a separate adjudication pass.
inc-103 is open and unruled, held for the design authority.
The frontend counts an animal as identified once one identifier is filled, matching V4's 'At least one Animal Identifier'.
Design release 1 counts an animal as entered only when every identifier has a value and lists only complete animals.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October ruling ranks first and answers this difference directly, withdrawing the earlier reading under which the 7 October ruling's prototype default made every identifier required. One identifier is enough: a live animal saved with at least one identifier is entered, listed in the saved table and moved past; the Complete status uses exactly the submit bar (optional with one species, at least one identified record per species with several), with no stricter every-animal bar; DR1 inc-103 is closed and not built. The same one-record bar applies to the germinal set's entries: a germinal entry counts once it holds at least one value, not merely because it was saved. This is what the service does today. repo-frontend-p6-019 and document-dr1-parity-backlog-p5-016 back the winning rule and are not overruled; ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-008 still stands as the general look-and-feel default and is not overruled. For the germinal set a lone species is not exempt: V4 asks for at least one germinal identifier per animal, so every selected germinal species, one or several, needs an entry holding at least one value (c-277).

conflicts.about: What a trader is told when they press a species panel's save with some or all of the animal's identifiers blank.

positions.says: One identifier is enough: a record with one identifier counts as identified.
Validation is a real constraint that overrides the prototype.
If every identifier is required, each empty box should name itself in the error summary, with new error copy, which DR1 does not supply.
A partly filled panel save keeps the same animal open with the values filled in and shows no error.
Save and finish with Passport blank and Ear tag filled does not save the animal and shows no error.
Save and finish with the passport blank does not save the animal, keeps the same panel open and shows no error.
An add with nothing entered shows 'Enter at least one identifier for this animal'; a partly filled animal saves.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October ruling ranks first: one identifier is enough, so a partly filled animal saves with no error and the panel moves on, setting aside DR2.1's hold on the same animal. DR1's per-identifier errors were asked for only if every identifier were ruled required, which the ruling closes (c-041), so they are not built and the earlier outcome that adopted them is withdrawn. An animal with no identifier at all is not a record: validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express (7 October ruling), so today's 'Enter at least one identifier for this animal', linked to the panel's first identifier field, stays where DR2.1 silently keeps the trader on the same animal; it is checked per panel. Save and continue and Save and return never block on missing identifiers, as in DR2.1. repo-frontend-p6-027 backs what is kept and is not overruled.

conflicts.about: What happens when a species' number of animals drops below its saved identification records.

positions.says: Keep the frontend's rule refusing a count lower than the records already entered, with its message (inc-094, Sam 2026-08-21).
Lowering the number of animals keeps the saved entries, and the table can list more animals than the new number.

conflicts.outcome: DR1 judged this same difference and ranks above the prototype. Commodity details refuses a count below the saved records with today's message and links to the species' panel; the over-count message stays as the safety net.
